results.name: CoreNet Global Begins a New Chapter with Incoming CEO Vicki Worden
results.content:
### CoreNet Global Begins a New Chapter with Incoming CEO Vicki Worden  
**Atlanta, GA – May 18, 2026** – CoreNet Global, the leading association for corporate real estate professionals, has named Vicki Worden, MBA, CAE, as its new Chief Executive Officer, effective August 1, 2026, following an extensive search process.  
Worden brings a strong history of transformative leadership and a proven track record of driving growth, innovation, and global impact to CoreNet Global. In her previous role as CEO of the Green Building Initiative (GBI), Worden transformed the organization into a thriving, internationally recognized leader in sustainability standards and building certification.  
Under Worden’s leadership, GBI experienced significant revenue growth, material increases in membership participation, and a strong increase in net assets. She spearheaded the acquisition and global expansion of GBI’s Green Globes certification program, significantly contributing to the certification of over one billion square feet of space worldwide through GBI’s suite of assessment programs.  
Worden is known for her entrepreneurial approach having launched innovative programs, such as the Journey to Net Zero (JNZ) carbon reduction assessment and the Better Buildings: Data Center Seminar, now a premier event at the intersection of sustainability and the data center sector. Her efforts have positioned GBI as a thought leader with its programs recognized by major organizations across the world.
Worden expressed her excitement for joining CoreNet Global: “I am thrilled to join CoreNet Global and build upon its strong legacy of global leadership, professional development, and industry connection. I am energized by the opportunity to help reinforce our organization’s position as the essential global platform where leaders come together to navigate what’s next for the corporate real estate profession.”  
CoreNet Global sincerely thanks Jeri Ballard, interim CEO, for her engagement, leadership, and commitment throughout this period of transition. Her efforts are greatly valued, and we extend our warmest wishes as she pursues future successes.  
With Worden’s appointment, CoreNet Global will build on the foundation Jeri Ballard established during the transition and continue delivering value to members and partners worldwide.  
**About CoreNet Global**  
CoreNet Global is the leading association for corporate real estate professionals, representing nearly 10,000 members in 50 countries worldwide. The organization provides education, networking, and research to support industry professionals in navigating workplace and business challenges. For more information, please visit corenetglobal.org.

results.name: August 2026 Newsletter | A New Leaf
results.content:
# August 2026 Newsletter  
**Hello friends and neighbors,**  
**After my first few months as CEO of A New Leaf, I continue to be inspired by thestaff,volunteers,donors,andcommunity partners who make our work possible.**I’vealso had the opportunity to meet clients whose resilience and determination remind me why this work matters so deeply.  
**This month’s newsletter shares the story of Kerlanda and Leon**, who both experienced homelessness and hardship before choosing a new path forward. After finding sobriety and beginning to rebuild their lives, they still faced a major challenge: finding safe, affordable housing where they could raise their children together. Through A New Leaf’s La Mesita Apartments, their family found the stability they needed to keep moving forward.  
Their story is remarkable, but it didn’t happen by chance.  
**It happened because compassionate donors believed families like theirs deserve the opportunity to rebuild.** It happened because dedicated staff and supporters helped make safe, affordable housing and family resources available when they needed them most. And it happened because Kerlanda and Leon chose to keep moving forward, working hard to maintain their sobriety, build careers, and create a better future for their children.  
That is what happens when a community comes together around a family determined to build a brighter future. **That is the power of A New Leaf.**
## August 2026 Donor Update: Your Legacy Matters  
A will is one of the most meaningful ways to care for the people and causes that matter most to you. It allows you to protect your loved ones, make your wishes clear, and create a lasting impact in your community.  
During Make-A-Will Month, A New Leaf is partnering with FreeWill to offer a simple online tool that allows you to create or update your legal will in about 20 minutes, completely free of charge. As you make your plans, you can also consider giving back by including a future gift to A New Leaf.  
A gift in your will can help ensure that generations of Valley families continue to have access to safe shelter, affordable housing, safety from domestic violence, and the support they need to build brighter futures.  
Every legacy gift helps carry A New Leaf’s mission of Helping Families, Changing Lives into the future. Take this important step for the people and causes you love. Create your free will today.  
**Visit A New Leaf’s Free Will page today**and discover how your generosity can make an even greater impact. If you have questions, please email Suzanne Percy, Senior Charitable Giving Advisor, at [spercy@turnanewleaf.org](https://turnanewleaf.org/august-2026-newsletter/mailto:spercy@turnanewleaf.org).
## August 2026 Community Partners Update: Creating Mighty Change Across the Valley  
**This month, A New Leaf celebrates Valley of the Sun United Way** (VSUW) for its longstanding partnership and commitment to strengthening communities across Maricopa County.  
VSUW has brought nonprofits, businesses, government agencies, donors, and community members together to address Maricopa County’s most pressing challenges for just over 100 years. Its current plan, **Mighty Change (MC) 2026**, focuses on four closely connected areas: health, housing and homelessness, education, and workforce development.  
**Through MC2026, VSUW is working to reduce food insecurity and homelessness**, expand access to affordable healthcare, improve third-grade reading proficiency, reconnect young people with school and employment, and help more community members secure higher-paying jobs.  
As one of VSUW’s key partner agencies, **A New Leaf plays a direct role in bringing MC2026 to life**. We advance many of these goals through shelter, housing assistance, affordable housing, food assistance, financial coaching, employment services, workforce training, and youth support. Together, our programming recognizes that stable housing, good health, education, and economic opportunity are deeply connected.

results.content:
Monday, August 11, 2025
# ABA News & Vision from the CEO’s Desk | August 2025  
Monday, August 11, 2025  
Dear ABA Members,  
Welcome to the launch of my monthly update. As I mark my fifth month as CEO of the ABA, I am amazed at how quickly the time has passed. I continue to be inspired by the passion, resilience, and innovation across our burn care community. From surgeons and nurses to researchers, rehabilitation specialists, first responders, and survivors, your work motivates me every single day. I remain committed to ensuring the ABA amplifies your voice and impact.  
This summer, under the leadership of ABA President Dr. Jeff Carter and the Board of Trustees, we officially launched the development of the ABA’s 2026–2028 Strategic Work Plan. Your input is shaping this collaborative process—through the updated member survey, Board liaison conversations with committee chairs, insights from ABA staff, and direct member engagement.  
Framed around five core pillars—Education, Research, Quality, Prevention, and Governance & Leadership—this roadmap will position the ABA for a bold, forward-looking future, focused on strengthening education, advancing advocacy, expanding research, and deepening engagement across the entire burn care community.
### **In the News: Burn Prevention Matters**  
This month’s national news offered a sobering reminder of why prevention remains central to our mission. On August 1 (New York Times), a 17-year-old visiting Yellowstone National Park suffered severe burns after stepping into a thin thermal crust near the Lone Star Geyser. The hot springs, which can exceed 185°F, pose significant risks for burn injuries and fatalities – especially for those who stray from the recommended paths.  
Incidents like this underscore the vital role of ABA in prevention, education, and advocacy. As we refine our strategic priorities, raising public awareness about burn risks—whether in homes, workplaces, or natural settings—remains essential. Visit these resources to learn more[.](https://www.ameriburn.org/news/prevention-in-action-lessons-from-yellowstone-severe-thermal-injury-underscores-the-need-for-awareness-and-caution)

From surgeons and nurses to researchers, rehabilitation specialists, first responders, and survivors, your work motivates me every single day. snippets.snippet: ### CoreNet Global Begins a New Chapter with Incoming CEO Vicki Worden **Atlanta, GA – May 18, 2026** – CoreNet Global, the leading association for corporate real estate professionals, has named Vicki Worden, MBA, CAE, as its new Chief Executive Officer, effective August 1, 2026, following an extensive search process. Worden brings a strong history of transformative leadership and a proven track record of driving growth, innovation, and global impact to CoreNet Global. In her previous role as CEO of the Green Building Initiative (GBI), Worden transformed the organization into a thriving, internationally recognized leader in sustainability standards and building certification. Under Worden’s leadership, GBI experienced significant revenue growth, material increases in membership participation, and a strong increase in net assets. She spearheaded the acquisition and global expansion of GBI’s Green Globes certification program, significantly contributing to the certification of over one billion square feet of space worldwide through GBI’s suite of assessment programs.
